annotations.title: Can you drink the tap water here?

description: Whether the tap water is drinkable, hamlet by hamlet (17 hamlets), from the guide's read of the water utility's and the state health department's own reporting. Three of the hamlets covered (Springs, Shelter Island, Southold) are private-well territory where no agency tests the water, and the record says so. Wainscott's record covers PFOS and PFOA found in more than 150 private wells and the December 2018 main extension that put the hamlet on public water. Every `safe` value refers to public water only; the guide holds no verdict on any private well. `verdict` is the guide's own paragraph for that hamlet. `status` comes with `statusMeaning`. `filterRecommendation` names a certification rather than a brand, with `filterCaveat` where the guide's glossary has corrected which NSF/ANSI number covers PFAS. `sources` are the citable links with the date each was read, including SCWA's June 2025 declaration of compliance with the federal PFOA/PFOS limits and the Stage 1 Water Alert declared across the East End on 14 July 2026, a drought conservation request whose own notice says supply and quality are unaffected. `utilities` names who pipes the water and a phone number, with no URL because the guide's filed links for those records no longer resolve. `noVerdictHeld` names a place the guide has not written up. `place` takes a hamlet, a region, or a ZIP. With no argument nothing is looked up and the answer lists the hamlets covered. `townScope` reports how the place argument was read; `townScope.recognized: false` means the name matched no East End place, the rows array is empty, and `didYouMean` lists near matches where any exist.

place.description: The place: a hamlet ('Montauk', 'Springs', 'Wainscott'), a region ('the Hamptons', 'North Fork'), or a ZIP ('11937'), in the asker's own words.
